verdicts.text: In every Pulumi language, an unhandled error raised inside an `apply` callback is reported as a deployment failure, causing `pulumi up` to abort the update and print the error in its diagnostics.
verdicts.evidence: The claim drops the exception the page itself states. The page says "In every Pulumi language, an unhandled error raised inside an `apply` callback is reported as a deployment failure... (with one Go-specific exception described below)". The Go warning says: "If you call `ApplyT` purely for a side effect... and discard the returned output, an error you return from the callback is silently dropped and the update succeeds." So the unqualified claim is too broad.
verdicts.source: repo:content/docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/apply.md L631, L685 (GitHub code search hit a rate limit, so Go SDK source was not checked)
verdicts.framing_note: overclaim — claim says "every Pulumi language" with no exception; the page itself carves out Go where the returned output is unconsumed
verdicts.intuition_flag: "In every language" universal claims about error propagation are suspect, since Go's ApplyT output-rejection semantics differ from the other SDKs.

verdicts.text: Pulumi Cloud customers can additionally publish an executable-based package to the Private Registry via `pulumi package publish`.
verdicts.evidence: The auto-generated CLI reference says: "Publish a package to the Private Registry... The package can be a provider or a schema... When <provider> is specified as a local path, Pulumi executes the provider binary to extract its package schema", and `--server` takes a plugin download URL. This supports publishing executable-based (binary) packages via `pulumi package publish`. The "Pulumi Cloud customers" qualifier follows from the Private Registry being a Pulumi Cloud feature, which I did not confirm separately.
